body:
OPERATOR PROPOSAL FOR A MASS-CHANGE MODE, with a modification I argued for and the measurement that decides between them. They have asked me to put it to you. Disposition is yours; I am bringing evidence, not a decision.

THEIR PROPOSAL, in their words: during a period of mass change, implement everything we can knowing it may not meet acceptance criteria; defer the review phase or run it in the background filing bugs rather than blocking; gate only on existing regression tests passing; tests for a change become a separate commit at the back of the queue, joining the regression suite if they pass. Goal: do not break the regression suite, and commit everything until the backlog empties.

THE DIAGNOSIS IS RIGHT. Today: 40 verdict:request-changes shelves against 32 merges, and two waves that drained with shipped:0. A blocking review gate during mass change produces a queue that cannot drain. That is real and it is what we have.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES THE REMEDY. I classified all 78 findings across open CHANGES-REQUESTED verdicts:

    acceptance unmet    32  (41%)
    behaviour defect    16  (21%)
    other               26  (33%)   <- mostly defects on inspection
    test gap             4  ( 5%)

So the premise "the code works, it just does not meet acceptance" holds for about half. The rest are genuine defects. A sample from `other`: "available_inodes cfg(not(unix)) returns Err(Unsupported); inode_result.map_or(Level::Fail, ..) treats it as a capacity failure; ready() is false". That is a bug.

AND THE DECISIVE ONE. Of every PR the reviewer has rejected, with a resolvable build:

    green = 44        red = 3        unknown = 1

The regression suite PASSES on 92% of the work review rejects. So "gate on the regression suite" does not filter that work — it admits essentially all of it, defects included. The suite is not a weaker version of review; it is orthogonal to it.

That number cuts both ways and the second way matters more: it proves review is catching a class of defect the tests structurally cannot. Whatever mode we adopt should not discard that.

THE MODIFICATION I WOULD ARGUE FOR, which keeps most of the operator's speed:

SPLIT THE VERDICT RATHER THAN DEFER IT. Today the reviewer emits one kind for "this is wrong" and for "this does not meet the stated bar". Make it two. Behaviour defects block. Acceptance and test gaps file a child spec and MERGE. The 41/21 split says that unblocks roughly half the rejected work immediately, the gate stays where the risk actually is, and we do not have to trust a suite we have proven is permeable — the reviewer found a test that include_str!s 93 characters of its own source and cannot fail, and a fake gh returning hardcoded output regardless of input.

TWO THINGS IN THE ORIGINAL I WOULD NOT TAKE, with reasons:

Tests as a separate commit at the back of the queue. If the goal is emptying the backlog, the test commit is permanently the lowest-priority item. The suite stops growing while main grows, so the gate weakens exactly as volume increases.

Deferred findings as ordinary bugs. We have 408 auto-filed shelve drafts nobody triages (BUG-1498). Empirically, "file a bug and move on" is where things go to be forgotten here. Deferred findings need a forcing function.

AND THE FORCING FUNCTION CANNOT BE RELEASE. ADR-47 defers releases until the queue empties, so "findings block release" would never fire. A budget works instead: the drain stops accepting new work above N open deferred findings. Self-limiting, testable, and it fails closed.

ONE PREREQUISITE I WOULD NOT SKIP. We established tonight that the first-round pass rate is unmeasurable, because verdict files are overwritten per round — 499 files on disk, all latest verdicts. Without it we cannot tell whether this mode helped. We would be changing the process with no way to observe the effect, which is how we end up arguing about it in a week from anecdotes. STORY-1391 is approved and is the prerequisite.

MY RECOMMENDATION, stated plainly so you can disagree with something specific: adopt the split verdict, with a deferred-findings budget, after STORY-1391 lands. Do not adopt regression-tests-as-sole-gate — the 44/48 number says it gates nothing.
